ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZbecGA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDCyOY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 31, "title": "Support sound port 0x95 clearing accesses and fast sweep", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `86aba6a037b153e14e3691548ea8f36bae23f4e9`, `bus.rs` rejects every IN/OUT to sound-test port `0x95`; `sound_tests.rs:84–86` explicitly requires even a zero write to fail. `audio.rs:93–100` implements only ordinary sweep timing.

The hardware-test source enables bit 1 for fast sweep and subsequently clears the port. Such software currently stops instead of continuing execution. No commercial-title benefit has been demonstrated.

## Expected outcome

WonderSwan, WonderSwan Color and SwanCrystal accept clearing writes and implement port `0x95` bit 1 fast sweep through the existing shared machine clock. Clearing the bit restores ordinary sweep. Support performs real frequency updates rather than merely suppressing the unsupported-port error.

This task covers fast sweep and its register interface. HOLD_CH and other debug functions remain explicit hardware-readiness gaps; completing this Issue does not establish complete port-95 or commercial-game compatibility.

## Context

- [Sound definitions](https://github.com/WonderfulToolchain/hardware-definitions/blob/46783132a59e576c11456f5997620594eca1c390/target/wswan/sound.xml) identify HOLD_CH at bit 0 and FAST_SWEEP at bit 1, describing the latter as bypassing the sweep clock divisor.
- [WSHWTest documentation](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSHWTest/blob/34e33d5bfaaabb8b09fa5a557e409efe9fbfd979/README.md#sound-sweep) describes enable prerequisites and sweep-time-write reset. Its [assembly experiment](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSHWTest/blob/34e33d5bfaaabb8b09fa5a557e409efe9fbfd979/WSHWTest.asm) checks fast sweep with time zero and clears `0x95` afterward. This is inspected experiment source, not an observed physical pass here.
- Upstream ares separates the fixed prescaler from the programmable sweep counter. This corroborates retaining the programmed counter when bypassing the prescaler, but does not independently establish silicon transition phase or hold semantics. Do not copy emulator code.
- Correction record: **old assumption:** all port-95 accesses, including zero, must fail. **Corrected requirement:** support established clearing and fast-sweep operations. **Rationale:** accessible hardware-experiment source contradicts blanket rejection. Replace the obsolete rejection assertion while preserving unrelated unsupported-port checks.
- Existing tooling includes Cargo, original CC0 NASM fixtures, Wasm builds and production-preview Chromium suites. Historical guidance describing a documentation-only repository is stale. [Saved validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/86aba6a037b153e14e3691548ea8f36bae23f4e9/docs/issue-29-validation.md) reports 90 core unit tests, 12 integration tests, one adapter test and both complete Chromium suites passing. Those results were not rerun during planning.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Before implementation, record a bounded source-to-behavior table covering fast-sweep clock selection, programmable sweep-time interaction, enable prerequisites, `0x8D` reset and entering/leaving fast mode. Distinguish direct experimental evidence, documentation-derived inference and provisional boundary policies. Correct mistaken AI-authored requirements with recorded primary evidence and rationale; no human approval or independent AI re-review is required.
- [ ] On all three models, accept writes `0x00` and `0x02` to `0x95`. Provide deterministic readback of supported control state, initially zero, explicitly documenting readback/reset values as emulator policy where unmeasured. Retain actionable, non-mutating diagnostics for unsupported bits rather than silently implementing HOLD_CH or accepting arbitrary debug controls.
- [ ] Implement fast sweep on the shared 3.072 MHz clock, including one frequency update per clock with sweep time zero, signed `0x8C` addition and 11-bit wrapping. Implement the reconciled programmable-time behavior. Clearing fast mode restores ordinary sweep; existing enable prerequisites and sweep-time-write reset remain covered. Do not change the audio sample rate or freeze unrelated channels/devices.
- [ ] Add independently calculated unit vectors for positive, negative and zero steps, both wrap directions, time zero and nonzero timing, enable combinations, reset, fast/normal transitions and unsupported-bit state preservation. Check exact update boundaries and equivalent results for single-clock versus chunked advancement, including a frame boundary. Label tests of provisional policies accordingly.
- [ ] Add an original source-included CC0 cartridge probe using real CPU IN/OUT instructions. On every model, native and production-player Wasm tests must observe successful clearing, fast frequency progression and restored ordinary operation through CPU-produced markers, plus measurable generated PCM. Cover restart/control reset and empty-after-drain behavior; do not substitute mocked registers or JavaScript synthesis.
- [ ] Preserve existing three-model gameplay, wavetable/voice/noise and speaker/headphone output, GDMA, SDMA/Hyper Voice, shared timing, input/orientation, raw cartridge identity, SRAM/cartridge EEPROM/internal EEPROM persistence and firmware-free startup. Keep the from-scratch ownership/provenance rules and browser-local ROM/save handling. Update hardware limitations, fixture provenance and relevant documentation without claiming hold support or observed commercial compatibility.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs and records pre-merge results for `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `git diff --check`; in `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against the production preview. Extend existing suites for this probe. Record failures, corrections, skips and the Coordinator's source-Issue review; resolve blocking findings before merge.

## Optional validation

Compare additional independently licensed sound experiments or exercise another browser engine when available. Record actual execution separately from inspected source. Commercial ROMs, proprietary firmware and human gameplay are unnecessary for acceptance.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
